title: The Comprehension Gap in LLM-Assisted Software Development: An Experiment
abstract: arXiv:2611.24216v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When LLM tools are pushed beyond their capabilities for software development tasks, developers must be able to step in. However, the comprehension that developers acquire during development might be negatively impacted due to excessive code generation. This could create a cognitive debt that needs to be resolved before tasks can be solved efficiently again. We explore how well developers understand code they generated by prompting in comparison to self-written and unseen code and how they reflect on their comprehension. We conduct a crossover experiment and interviews with 35 participants consisting of students, academic personnel, and software developers. After completing two programming tasks with or without LLM chat usage, respectively, participants are tasked with finding introduced mutations in the produced and additional unseen code. translated_title: LLM辅助软件开发中的理解差距：一项实验研究
translated_abstract: 当LLM工具在软件开发任务中被推向超出其能力范围时，开发者必须能够及时介入。然而，由于过度的代码生成，开发者在开发过程中所获得的理解可能会受到负面影响。这可能造成一种“认知债务”，需要先加以解决才能重新高效地完成任务。我们探索了开发者对自己通过提示词生成的代码的理解程度（与自写代码和未见过的代码进行对比），以及他们如何反思自身的理解水平。我们对35名参与者（包括学生、学术人员和软件开发者）开展了交叉实验和访谈。参与者分别在使用和不使用LLM聊天工具的条件下完成两个编程任务，随后需要在所生成的代码以及额外的未见过的代码中找出被引入的变异。我们结合访谈和屏幕录像的洞察来补充实验结果。
tldr: 通过35名参与者的交叉实验发现，开发者对LLM生成代码的理解显著低于自写代码，这种“认知债务”会阻碍后续任务的高效完成。
